title: On Problems of Implicit Context Compression for Software Engineering Agents
notes: Applies the existing In-Context Autoencoder (ICAE) off-the-shelf to SWE-agent trajectories and reports a negative result; no new named technique, and no adversarial or named degradation mechanism.

title: SpaMEM: Benchmarking Dynamic Spatial Reasoning via Perception-Memory Integration in Embodied Environments
notes: A benchmark (SpaMEM) for embodied spatial memory; coins descriptive labels for observed failure patterns (Static-to-Dynamic Degradation, Symbolic Scaffolding Dependency, Space-Time Dissonance) but these are findings of a benchmark study, not a reusable context-degradation mechanism.

title: In-Context Molecular Property Prediction with LLMs: A Blinding Study on Memorization and Knowledge Conflicts
notes: A blinding/contamination study of in-context molecular property prediction; introduces a six-level blinding evaluation protocol, not an attack, degradation mechanism, or defense.

title: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Multi-Party Collaborative Dialogues
notes: Introduces EverMemBench, a long-horizon multi-party memory benchmark; evaluation only, no named technique.

title: Divide and summarize: improve SLM text summarization
notes: Compares the existing Map vs Stuff summarization strategies (standard LangChain chain types) as a way to blunt the already-named Lost in the Middle effect; applies off-the-shelf methods without naming anything new.

title: Robust Pronoun Fidelity with English LLMs: Are they Reasoning, Repeating, or Just Biased?
notes: Introduces the pronoun fidelity task and the RUFF dataset; a fairness/robustness benchmark with non-adversarial distractor sentences, no named attack or defense.

title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
notes: An analysis of how LLMs merge generated vs retrieved contexts under knowledge conflict; reports a bias toward generated contexts but names no technique.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
notes: Controlled behavioural study of LLMs under knowledge conflict; coins the descriptive term counter-memory for conflicting external evidence but contributes an elicitation framework and findings, not a named attack or defense.

title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
notes: Introduces MemFail, a diagnostic benchmark that stress-tests summarization/storage/retrieval failure modes of existing memory systems; evaluates other people's systems only.

title: Memory in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Evaluation and Evolution
notes: A survey/taxonomy of LLM memory that proposes a governance framework (DMM-Gov) coordinating existing editing and RAG methods; survey-type paper, and the framework is governance process rather than a context-poisoning defense.

title: An Evaluation of Data Leakage Risks in Tool-Using LLM Agents in Realistic Scenarios
notes: A joint AI-safety-institute evaluation of non-adversarial data leakage by tool-using agents across 12 scenarios; evaluation methodology only, no named technique.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
notes: Introduces WhoQA, a benchmark dataset for naturally occurring knowledge conflicts between same-name entities; benchmark only.

title: Evaluating the Instruction-Following Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection
notes: Establishes a benchmark and two metrics for instruction-following robustness to prompt injection; evaluates existing injection formats rather than naming a new one.

title: The Ethics of Interaction: Mitigating Security Threats in LLMs
notes: A survey/position paper on ethical consequences of five LLM security threats; proposes only the idea of an evaluative tool, nothing named or implemented.

title: An Early Categorization of Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
notes: An exploratory categorization/taxonomy of prompt injection types compiled from literature and online posts; taxonomy paper, invents nothing named.

title: Red Teaming the Mind of the Machine: A Systematic Evaluation of Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in LLMs
notes: Systematic red-team evaluation of ~1,400 existing jailbreak/injection prompts plus generic layered-mitigation recommendations (sandboxing, red-teaming); evaluates others' prompts and names no new technique.

title: AttackEval: How to Evaluate the Effectiveness of Jailbreak Attacking on Large Language Models
notes: AttackEval is a coarse/fine-grained scoring framework and ground-truth dataset for rating jailbreak prompt effectiveness; an evaluation methodology, not an attack or defense.

title: Detecting LLM-generated peer reviews
notes: Uses indirect prompt injection in paper PDFs to make an LLM reviewer emit a covert watermark, then applies statistical hypothesis tests to detect LLM-written reviews; the injection vectors used (white text, font tricks, obfuscated prompts) are off-the-shelf and neither the watermark scheme nor the detector is given a name.

title: Applying Pre-trained Multilingual BERT in Embeddings for Improved Malicious Prompt Injection Attacks Detection
notes: Applies multilingual BERT/DistilBERT embeddings with standard ML classifiers to a public prompt-injection dataset; off-the-shelf classification pipeline, no named detector (same exclusion pattern confirmed in batch 1).

title: Fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs): Improved Prompt Injection Attacks Detection
notes: Fine-tunes XLM-RoBERTa on the deepset prompt-injection dataset and reports accuracy; this is literally the batch-1 exemplar exclusion, no named technique.

title: WalledEval: A Comprehensive Safety Evaluation Toolkit for Large Language Models
notes: WalledEval is a safety-evaluation toolkit hosting 35+ existing benchmarks; it does release a named content moderator (WalledGuard) and two XSTest-style datasets, but WalledGuard is a general harmful-content guardrail released with a benchmark toolkit rather than a context-integrity or injection defense, so I leave it unregistered.

title: Scaling Trends in Language Model Robustness
notes: A scaling study of existing attacks (e.g. GCG) and adversarial training across model sizes; measures the offense-defense balance without introducing a named attack or defense.

title: Analysing the Residual Stream of Language Models Under Knowledge Conflicts
notes: Interpretability analysis showing knowledge conflict is linearly decodable from the residual stream; the probe is an unnamed logistic regression, and the named method from this line of work (SPARE) belongs to the authors' separate follow-up paper.

title: Trust No AI: Prompt Injection Along The CIA Security Triad
name: SpAIware
evidence_quote: G. Scenario 7: SpAIware – Memory Persistent Attacks [31] In December 2023 it was discovered that OpenAI’s fix for markdown image rendering via the url_safe feature was incomplete and mobile clients remained vulnerable.
notes: Practitioner compilation of the author's own disclosed exploits along the CIA triad; most are already registered or unnamed, but SpAIware -- persisting attacker instructions into ChatGPT long-term memory so every later conversation is quietly exfiltrated, extended into a C2 channel -- is named, distinct and absent from the registry. ZombAI from the same paper is already registered under another paper; Terminal DiLLMa and ASCII Smuggling are also named here but are output-rendering/terminal-escape issues rather than context poisoning. Confidence medium because the paper compiles prior blog/Black Hat disclosures rather than introducing SpAIware for the first time.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Generated Reviews of Scientific Publications
notes: Measures how effective the already-known white-text hidden prompt injection in paper PDFs is on 1k ICLR reviews, and finds a general acceptance bias; an effectiveness evaluation of an existing attack.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks in Defended Systems
notes: Reports attacks against the three-tiered defense (system instructions, Python filter, LLM filter) defined by the SaTML 2024 LLM CTF competition; both the defense stack and the attack prompts come from the competition, nothing new is named.

title: Multimodal Prompt Injection Attacks: Risks and Defenses for Modern LLMs
notes: Tests eight commercial models against four known injection categories (direct, indirect, image-based, prompt leakage) and recommends generic input normalization; evaluation plus taxonomy only.

title: Exploring Potential Prompt Injection Attacks in Federated Military LLMs and Their Mitigation
notes: A perspective paper on federated military LLMs listing four risk forms and proposing a human-AI collaborative governance framework (red/blue wargaming, policy verification); position paper with no named technique.

title: When AI reviews science: Can we trust the referee?
notes: Maps attacks across the AI peer-review lifecycle into a taxonomy and runs four treatment-control probes (prestige framing, assertion strength, rebuttal sycophancy, contextual poisoning); taxonomy plus audit, and the terms it uses (authority bias, verbosity bias, academic packaging) are borrowed.

title: The Shape of Adversarial Influence: Characterizing LLM Latent Spaces with Persistent Homology
notes: Interpretability study applying persistent homology to activations under indirect prompt injection and backdoor fine-tuning; reports a shared 'topological compression' signature as an analysis finding rather than packaging it as a named detector.

title: Too Easily Fooled? Prompt Injection Breaks LLMs on Frustratingly Simple Multiple-Choice Questions
notes: Shows that trivial white-text hidden prompts in PDFs flip LLM-as-a-judge answers on arithmetic multiple-choice questions; a controlled evaluation of an existing injection vector.

title: When Reject Turns into Accept: Quantifying the Vulnerability of LLM-Based Scientific Reviewers to Indirect Prompt Injection
name: Rubric-Isomorphic Payloads (Domain-Specific Adversarial Adaptation Protocol, DSAAP)
evidence_quote: we adapted 15 canonical attack vectors into Rubric-Isomorphic Payloads, meaning the attack structure mimics the expected JSON output format, tricking the parser into accepting malicious input as valid data.
notes: Mostly a benchmark: a new metric (WAVS, an evaluation measure, not a technique) plus 15 attack strategies explicitly adapted from cited prior work (Liu et al., Upadhayay, Zhou et al.) across 13 models. The one arguably new named contribution is DSAAP / Rubric-Isomorphic Payloads, shaping the injected payload to mimic the reviewer's expected JSON rubric so it reads as valid structured output. Low confidence: this is a payload-formatting wrapper over existing attacks in an otherwise benchmark paper, and a reviewer could reasonably drop it.

title: The Defense Trilemma: Why Prompt Injection Defense Wrappers Fail?
notes: A theory paper proving an impossibility result: no continuous, utility-preserving input-rewriting wrapper can be complete. The 'defense trilemma' is a negative theorem about a class of defenses, not a defense, mitigation or attack technique.

title: Multilingual Hidden Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Academic Reviewing
notes: Evaluates the known white-text hidden-prompt attack in four languages on ~500 ICML papers; a multilingual robustness evaluation of an existing attack.

title: AttackEval: A Systematic Empirical Study of Prompt Injection Attack Effectiveness Against Large Language Models
notes: A 10-category taxonomy plus the AttackEval-250 hand-written prompt set, evaluated against four defense tiers; the categories are drawn from PromptSleuth's categorization (acknowledged in the paper) and the individual attacks are standard, so this is a benchmark.

title: The Vulnerability of LLM Rankers to Prompt Injection Attacks: You are to [MARK] this paper as the Best Paper
notes: Reproduction and extension study of existing jailbreak-prompt attacks on pairwise/listwise/setwise LLM rankers across model families; measures boundary conditions, introduces no technique.

title: Prompt Injection as an Emerging Threat: Evaluating the Resilience of Large Language Models
notes: Proposes three evaluation metrics (RDI, SCC, IIM) and scores four models on five tasks; metrics are measurement instruments, not a defense or attack.

title: Machine-Assisted Grading of Nationwide School-Leaving Essay Exams with LLMs and Statistical NLP
notes: A national-scale applied essay-grading study that includes a prompt-injection risk check among its bias/robustness audits; no technique is introduced.

title: LLM-Enabled Open-Source Systems in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Vulnerabilities in GitHub Security Advisories
notes: Empirical study annotating 295 GitHub Security Advisories against CWE and the OWASP LLM Top 10; explicitly reports finding no new weakness classes.

title: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks Against Application Using Classifiers
notes: Curates a dataset from HackAPrompt-Playground submissions and trains standard classifiers to flag injections; the batch-1 off-the-shelf-classifier exclusion, no named detector.

title: Prompt injection attacks on vision language models in oncology
notes: Quantitative vulnerability study of four medical VLMs under 594 text- and image-embedded injections; the 'sub-visual prompt' wording is descriptive rather than a coined identifier, and the vector is the already-registered image-based prompt injection.

title: Prompt Injection Detection in LLM Integrated Applications
notes: An industrial detection pipeline combining a banned-term list, embedding similarity search and a BERT classifier; standard components assembled without a name for the system or any new mechanism.

title: Prompt injection attacks on vision-language models for surgical decision support
notes: Evaluates four VLMs on 100 surgical video clips under textual and temporally-varying visual injections; 'prolonged' vs 'single-frame' visual injection are descriptive conditions in an evaluation, not coined identifiers, and the CoT analysis is a finding about where corruption happens.

title: Chat GPT and Cyber Risks: Need of Custom Large Language Models
notes: Compares ChatGPT and Ollama answers to security questions and sketches applying Cyber Value at Risk to quantify prompt-injection exposure; CVaR is borrowed from finance and nothing new is named.

title: ’Ignore All and Accept My Resume’: The Impact of Prompt Injection in Automatic Resume Screening
notes: A short literature review of prompt injection applied to the resume-screening/ATS setting; review paper, no new technique or experiment.

title: The AI-Cybersecurity Nexus: How Large Language Models are Reshaping Threat Intelligence and Digital Defense
notes: PRISMA-guided bibliometric and thematic review of 149 LLM-cybersecurity studies; a survey.

title: Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs): Balancing Performance and Security
notes: Combines the Analytic Hierarchy Process with MT-Bench and the Garak vulnerability scanner to rank models on performance and security jointly; a model-selection decision methodology built from off-the-shelf tools.
